integrated_description: Emma and Alex engage in a structured, honest dialogue—free of ultimatums—to collaboratively establish specific, measurable boundaries around Alex's friendship with his ex: defining acceptable one-on-one contact frequency, types of communication (e.g., no hidden DMs, no late-night or alcohol-context meetups), and an emotional exclusivity standard preventing the ex from becoming a primary emotional outlet or surrogate partner. A clear transparency protocol is agreed upon—covering what is proactively shared versus kept private—with scheduled check-ins every 4–8 weeks to assess whether Emma's sense of safety is improving and Alex's autonomy is preserved, ensuring all boundaries serve emotional safety rather than control or humiliation of any party. If good-faith agreements are repeatedly violated or negotiation fails to produce felt safety, a defined escalation path applies: mandatory renegotiation first, then treating violations as trust breaches requiring deeper intervention, and as a last resort, revisiting contact levels up to and including distancing—with non-compliance addressed directly at each stage rather than allowed to drift into resentment.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders converged on the same core demands—measurable behavioral standards, a concrete transparency protocol, time-bound review periods, dignity protections, and a clear escalation path with stated consequences—making full integration feasible without sacrificing the original synthesis's non-ultimatum, collaborative ethos. The escalation path satisfies stakeholder_c's explicit requirement while the dignity and autonomy protections satisfy stakeholder_b, and the specificity of contact rules and revisit clauses satisfies stakeholder_a.
